citations.excerpt: The Southern delegates held a convention at Louisville , Kentucky , in 1845, at which the "Methodist Episcopal Church, South" was formed.
The withdrawal of the slave-holding states from the general body now appeared unavoidable, and a "Plan of Separation" was elaborated and accepted.
In 1939 the Methodist Episcopal Church (South), the Methodist Protestant Church, and the Methodist Episcopal Church united into the Methodist Church

facts.value: Formed when the Methodist Episcopal Church divided over slavery after the 1844 General Conference dispute over a slaveholding bishop, under a Plan of Separation.
